topic: Aurora frame interpolation: flicker and missing textures fixed, NVIDIA frame limiter detection, optional low-latency mode
report: User and a friend saw flicker and vanishing textures with interpolation; user now has a 120 Hz primary monitor.
root_causes: Every sealed batch held the end of game frame k, its display copy and the start of frame k+1 (36 draws on average in the hangar replay). Slot replays drew the k+1 head into the EFB the native image continued from, so the native image mixed two game frames; slots mixed an uninterpolated head with an interpolated tail; matching per batch lost or swapped partners when the cut moved.
SSAO (default on), floor reflections and light shafts were applied to the native image only, alternating every other image at 120 Hz.
CMPR decodes and palette conversions ran only in the native render, which is encoded after the slots.
User PC: NVIDIA global profile Max Frame Rate = 60 (user set) and Low Latency On. Present slept ~10 ms per call with the GPU at 14 %, so nothing above 60 could ever reach the screen.
changes: gfx/common.cpp: with interpolation on, passes after the last display copy are carried to the next batch and drawn first by all its images; two alternating GPU buffer sets (80 MB extra, created on first carry), RenderPass::bufferSet; scene effects in slots of self-contained frames; decodes in the first image of a group, palette conversions in every image.

gx/frame_interpolation.cpp: matching and cadence per game frame (boundary = display copy), head and tail of a frame matched against the same previous frame with claims kept across seals; camera cut detection (>=40 % of >=16 static pairs jump >35 deg or >5 m).
aurora.cpp: slots replay only when the sealed batch starts a game frame; optional low-latency path (native encoded and published first, slots extrapolated at weight 1 + w).

runtime dxgi_frame_latency.cpp: read-only NvAPI DRS read of Max Frame Rate for this executable ([frame-limit] log); settings_overlay.cpp keeps interpolation off at <=61 and caps the target otherwise, with an F1 note; new F1 checkbox and [video] frame_interpolation_low_latency.
QA-only switches: WII_COMPILED_QA_INTERP_WEIGHT_ONE, _COMPARE_EVERY, _NO_CARRY; _IGNORE_MONITOR also ignores the driver cap.
recomp/tools/nvidia_game_profile.py check|create|delete: per-executable NVIDIA profile with the limiter off. create was NOT run (blocked by the permission classifier; the user decides).

pixel_equality_weight_one.old_no_carry: 385/699 identical, worst 48 % of pixels strongly different, 73 groups above 1 %
